thread.title: NCCC gets major equipment donation to start new CDL program - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: NCCC gets major equipment donation to start new CDL program - NewsBreak

author: KOAMNewsNowcom KOAMTV
title: NCCC gets major equipment donation to start new CDL program - NewsBreak
text:
12 hours ago CHANUTE, Kan. (KOAM) - Neosho County Community College has received a large equipment donation from Old Dominion Freight Line to help start the college’s new commercial driver’s license training program. The CDL program is expected to begin in fall 2026.
The donation includes:
Two 2019 Freightliner tractors One 2009 Wabash 48-foot trailer Two Wabash 28-foot trailers One 2006 Wabash converter/dolly College leaders said the equipment will give students hands-on training on industry-standard vehicles as they work toward earning a CDL and entering the trucking and transportation field.
“We are incredibly grateful to Old Dominion Freight Line for this generous donation,” NCCC President Dr. Brian Inbody said in a statement. He said there is high demand for qualified commercial drivers and the donated equipment will help students gain real-world experience.
The college said the program is being developed to meet workforce needs in southeast Kansas and nearby areas. Students will receive classroom instruction and behind-the-wheel training to prepare for CDL licensure and jobs in transportation.
Old Dominion said it is proud to support the program and plans to connect with students during the training to offer guidance and share industry insights.
More information about the fall 2026 CDL program is available at neosho.edu by clicking the CDL banner.
You can also call NCCC’s Outreach and Workforce Development Division at (620) 432-0406 for details.
